newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Lufthansa sees cargo growth in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa sees cargo growth in Hungary.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Friday it aimed to boost its cargo trade by as much as 15 percent at Budapest Ferihegy Airport in 1997.
"I would like to increase our business around 10 to 15 percent this year," Peter Mojen, director of the Budapest office of the airline's subsidiary Lufthansa Cargo AG, told Reuters.
Lufthansa, the biggest cargo carrier in Hungary among foreign airlines, increased its cargo shipments from Ferihegy some 30 percent to 880 tonnes in 1996 from 680 tonnes in 1995, Mojen said.
The airline's shipments to Budapest were nearly steady at 2,742 tonnes in 1996 from 2,756 tonnes, he added.

"The Hungarian government has been discouraging imports and encouraging exports to improve its trade balance, but this policy has been easing, so the market should strengthen in both directions this year," Mojen said.
Roughly 90 percent of Lufthansa's cargo traffic at Ferihegy originates on routes through Frankfurt, while the remaining 10 percent is carried on flights via Duesseldorf and Munich, Mojen added.
Lufthansa has focused its business in Budapest on destinations to the Far East and South America, Mojen said, noting that common shipments include car parts to Brazil and goose liver to Japan.
The airline has increased its flexibility to carry cargo between Budapest and Frankfurt by adding to its summer flight schedule a third daily flight on the route with an Airbus A319.
"Theoretically, this means we have added 1.7 tonnes of cargo capacity," Mojen said. "Practically, this means we will have only another 1.3-1.5 tonnes because of the volume of passenger baggage."
Lufthansa already operates two daily flights between Budapest and Frankfurt -- one on an Airbus A320, the other on a Boeing 737, he added.

The German airline also wants to expand its road shipments between Budapest and Frankfurt in cooperation with Hungarian national airline Malev Rt, which is owned 30 percent by Italian state airline Alitalia, Mojen said.
Lufthansa already carries cargo on this route with a 20-tonne-payload truck on Mondays and Thursdays, and Malev operates a similar truck on Wednesday, he said.
The two airlines have been negotiating the terms to operate trucks jointly on Tuesdays and Fridays, he added.
Lufthansa takes roughly half of incoming cargo and 20 percent of outgoing cargo at Ferihegy by truck, Mojen said.
"We are using more and more trucks," Mojen said. "Our shipments are changing to include bigger and heavier pieces of cargo that are not appropriate for the bulk-load planes that we fly to Budapest."

Occasionally, Lufthansa also flies extra-heavy cargo from Budapest, Mojen said, noting it recently carried several 1.1-tonne axles from Hungarian commercial vehicle company Raba Magyar Vagon es Gepgyar Rt.
Lufthansa had to switch aircraft on one of its Frankfurt flights to an Airbus A300-600 to carry the axles, which were transferred in Germany onto a Boeing 747 cargo plane flying to Chicago, he said.
